subject: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated follow-up
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated follow-up

Hi Jamie / Taylor,

Thanks again for the time this morning — useful discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Call recap:
- Workload: inference for conversational agents + reranking. You mentioned ~300 requests/sec peak, ~350 tokens per request on average.
- Primary concern: noisy-neighbor effects on shared pools causing latency spikes impacting customer SLAs.
- Requirements: predictable p95 latency, isolation for high-priority customers, and ability to burst for launches.
- Regulatory: some telemetry needs to be retained for 12 months; no hard on-prem mandate today but could be required for specific customers later.

Qualification notes / options we discussed:
1) Hosted API (shared): fastest to get started, cost-efficient, automatic batching/caching. Good if you can tolerate occasional noisy-neighbor tail latency and don't need strict isolation.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for your account with isolation guarantees and configurable SLOs — reduces noisy-neighbor risk and gives predictable throughput.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation and customer-managed control plane for strict regulatory/air-gap requirements.

Requested items / next steps:
- Can you confirm the numbers above (peak requests/sec, avg tokens per request, expected daily QPS)? These drive capacity estimates.
- We will share a short doc outlining the Dedicated SLA + isolation guarantees and a copy of our SOC 2 report. (Attaching SLA draft + SOC2.)
- Technical deep-dive: would like to schedule a 60-min infra session with Marissa (cc'd) to walk through isolation mechanics (noisy neighbor mitigations, KV cache behavior, eviction policies, autoscale headroom). Proposed slots: Thu 3/25 10:00–11:00 PST or Fri 3/26 9:00–10:00 PST.
- Pricing/estimate: we'll provide a preliminary dedicated sizing + cost estimate after you confirm traffic profile and models.

If you want, include an internal customer example we can map to — happy to do a sizing exercise on the call.

Thanks,
Priyom
--

Thanks, Priyom — quick confirmation and a couple follow-ups.

Numbers: 
- Peak: ~300 requests/sec (this is bursty during peak hours; sustained average ~120 rps).
- Avg tokens per request: ~350 tokens (post-trimming).
- P95 requirement: ideally < 500ms for user-facing requests; background jobs can be higher.

Why dedicated: our product team experienced tail latency spikes on shared infra during a recent launch (other vendors' shared endpoints). We need predictable latency for our SLA customers and want to avoid noisy-neighbor risk.

Questions: 
1) In your Dedicated offer, do you guarantee isolation at the GPU level or is it a tenant-on-node model?
2) How do KV cache and prefix caching work across tenants on shared pools? Are caches tenant-specific?
3) If we start on Dedicated, how easy is it to move to Private VPC later if a customer requires it?

We'd like the SLA and SOC2 — appreciate the attachments. Also: can you give a rough cost delta between a dedicated pool sized for our peak vs expanded shared with higher-priority routing?

We can do Thu 3/25 10:00 PST for the deep-dive. Sending over an internal doc with traffic patterns in a follow-up.

—Jamie
Director of Product, Acme Robotics
jamie@acmerobotics.com

Jamie — thanks for the details and for confirming Thu the 25th. Answers inline and attachments included.

On Tue, Mar 22, 2027 at 9:15 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:
> Call recap:
> - Workload: inference for conversational agents + reranking. You mentioned ~300 requests/sec peak, ~350 tokens per request on average.

Direct answers to your questions: 
1) Isolation model for Dedicated: we provide tenant-dedicated pools — customers get reserved GPU capacity (logical tenant isolation). Workloads are scheduled onto GPUs reserved for your pool, so noisy neighbors from other accounts are eliminated on that pool. We can discuss physically-dedicated nodes for the highest security/latency needs, but the standard Dedicated product provides logical isolation + resource reservation.

2) Caching behavior: KV cache and prefix caching are tenant-scoped when you run in Dedicated or Private. On Shared/Hosted API, caching is multi-tenant but keys are namespaced per tenant; that reduces cross-tenant pollution but does not provide the same eviction/latency guarantees as Dedicated.

3) Migration path to Private: yes — we support a staged migration. Customers frequently start on Dedicated, then move to Private VPC (same control plane, different networking and KMS integration). We'll capture required network/IPs and onboarding steps in the deep-dive.

Preliminary sizing notes (rough): with 300 rps peak and 350 tokens/request, assuming standard batching and KV cache hit rates ~30%, we'd estimate starting with a small dedicated pool (2–4 A100-class GPUs) and scale from there. We'll finalize after we see your exact concurrency profiles (peak concurrency, tail QPS per minute).

I've attached:
- redwood_dedicated_vs_shared_sla.pdf — draft SLA and isolation guarantees (high level).
- SOC2-report-2026.pdf — summary of controls.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (60 min):
- 15 min: infra overview (isolation, scheduling, autoscale) — Marissa
- 20 min: telemetry & SLOs (p95/p99 measurement, alerting, cost/latency tradeoffs) — Priyom
- 20 min: sizing + migration path & next steps

Possible agenda addition: if you want, share a sanitized sample of a 1-hour traffic trace before the call and Marissa can sketch a capacity plan live.

Action items for you before Thu:
- Send the 1-hour peak trace (CSV with timestamp, requests/sec, avg tokens) if available.
- Confirm if you need physical node isolation (we can suggest options during the call).

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Priyom
